q: Does the DSB complexity distribution (not just total DSB number) explain the LET-scaling of misrejoining/mutation better than total DSB yield does?
basis: Friedland 2012 encodes complexity implicitly via slow-channel saturation but never publishes the DSB-complexity distribution shape parameters PARTRAC generates; the paper's phenomenology therefore cannot be decomposed into a 'yield' vs 'complexity' contribution.
next_steps: Run Geant4-DNA at UICGPU for 5 ion species (H, He, C, N, Fe) x 5 energies each, extract per-DSB complexity histograms (adjacent SSB count, base damage density).
Fit a two-component NHEJ Gillespie model where the slow rate constant is a function of DSB complexity bin, not aggregate LET.
Cross-validate against KURBUC and RITRACKS on identical target geometries and compare misrejoining probability vs total DSB and vs mean complexity.

q: How much does an NHEJ repair model output diverge across three independent stochastic track-structure codes (PARTRAC vs Geant4-DNA vs KURBUC) when fed the same Friedland-2012 NHEJ rules?
basis: PARTRAC is closed; no independent group has run a rigorous cross-code test of Friedland's exact NHEJ formulation. Published paper-to-paper comparisons conflate physics differences with chemistry/biology differences.
next_steps: Implement the Friedland 2012 NHEJ rules (fast/slow rejoining with complexity-dependent slow-channel capacity + labile-site delayed detection) as a standalone open Gillespie library.
Drive the library first with Geant4-DNA-generated DSB end lists, then with KURBUC-generated DSB end lists, and diff rejoining kinetics at 15 min / 1 h / 4 h / 24 h.
Publish the Gillespie library on GitHub with a full test-suite so any group can reproduce and extend the cross-code comparison.

q: How sensitive are the fast and slow NHEJ rate constants to chromatin geometry (fiber compaction, loop-domain topology, hetero- vs euchromatin), and does the paper's 'two rate constants suffice' claim survive when chromatin state is varied?
basis: Friedland 2012 assumes a stylised chromatin model inside PARTRAC. Hi-C-derived polymer models show DSB proximity statistics depend strongly on chromatin state; if so, part of what Friedland attributes to biochemistry may be geometry.
next_steps: Use a Hi-C-informed polymer simulator (chromatin3D or OpenMiChroM) to sample DSB end proximity graphs for euchromatin- and heterochromatin-enriched regions.
Drive the open Gillespie NHEJ library (from Q2) with those proximity graphs and refit fast/slow rate constants.
Report the fractional change in fitted rate constants between chromatin states and test whether the two-component sufficiency claim breaks (i.e., needs a third component or a state-dependent rate).

q: What fraction of the phenomenological 'labile-site delayed detection' is really delayed enzymatic conversion of clustered non-DSB lesions (base damage, SSB clusters, DSB with adjacent lesions), rather than pure enzyme kinetics on prompt DSBs?
basis: Friedland 2012 introduces a labile-site amplitude but does not decompose it by underlying lesion type. Distinguishing enzyme kinetics from lesion-conversion kinetics is a key open question for both photon and ion RBE modelling.
next_steps: Run Geant4-DNA with chemistry stage enabled to enumerate sub-DSB clustered lesion densities per LET.
Fit a three-population NHEJ model (prompt-DSB / labile-converted DSB / clustered-lesion converted DSB) to photon and ion rejoining kinetics.
Test whether the fitted labile amplitude scales with the Geant4-DNA-predicted clustered-lesion density across the LET grid.

q: Does the Friedland 2012 NHEJ model extrapolate to the FLASH ultra-high-dose-rate regime (>40 Gy/s), and if not, what minimal extension is needed?
basis: FLASH may alter DSB production and repair via transient oxygen depletion or radical recombination, phenomena absent from PARTRAC's conventional kinetics. The paper predates FLASH and does not comment. This has become a highly active question in radiotherapy.
next_steps: Literature-scan FLASH-vs-conventional DSB rejoining measurements (Vozenin, Favaudon, Loo groups) and build a small open dataset.
Add a dose-rate-dependent oxygen-depletion and radical-recombination term to the open Gillespie NHEJ library and test whether the two-component + labile skeleton still fits FLASH kinetics.
Cross-check against Geant4-DNA-Chem simulations with explicit radiolytic species and against experimental transient pO2 measurements.
